name: stri_split_lines1
title: Split a String Into Text Lines

origin.description: Split one string into lines and drop a final empty line.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A single string. A longer vector warns and uses the first element.

origin.details: Equivalent to splitting the first string on the same newline sequences as stri_split_lines, then omitting the empty field after a final newline. An empty line before that final newline is kept. A missing string is NA. An empty vector is an error.
origin.example:
parts <- stri_split_lines1("a
b
")
cat(paste0('stri_split_lines1("a\nb\n") returns ', paste(parts, collapse = ", "), '.
'))

translation.description: Split one string into lines and drop a final empty line.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: One string, or a list whose first element is used. An empty vector is an error.

translation.details: Splits on CR, LF, CRLF, NEL, VT, FF, U+2028, and U+2029. A trailing newline does not add an empty field. An empty line earlier in the string is kept. A missing string is a one-element NA vector. An empty vector is an error. A longer vector warns and uses the first element.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing string is a one-element NA vector.
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_split_lines1
parts = stri_split_lines1("a\nb\n")
print('stri_split_lines1("a\\nb\\n") returns ' + ", ".join(parts) + ".")
